text.p: British water company Severn Trent Plc said on Wednesday that trading so far this year has been "satisfactory".
Chairman Richard Ireland told the company's annual meeting that order books for the non-regulated businesses were healthy.

He also said the British government's levy on utilities would not affect the company's policies. The firm, however, did not disclose how much the windfall tax imposed by the government on privatised utilities would cost the firm.
Severn Trent and United Utilities Plc are the only privatised utilities that have not yet published the expected costs of the tax.

Chancellor Gordon Brown imposed the one-off tax at the budget on July 2 and plans to raise around 2.1 billion pounds from the electricity sector, some 1.65 billion from water companies and another 1.45 billion from other privatised utilities.
